patterns_discovered.description: Functions organized by operation type: list (read), detail (read), create (write), send (state change), confirm (state change), item_add (write), item_remove (delete)
All write operations return JsonResponse with success flag, message, and optional data (order_id, item_id, redirect_url)
Generic try-except blocks wrapping all logic with exception message returned in JsonResponse
Functions check order.status before allowing mutations (DRAFT for edits, SENT for confirm)
Use of select_related() and prefetch_related() for reducing database queries
Decimal type used for monetary values (unit_price, quantity calculations)
All write operations store created_by and updated_by with request.user
Multiple Q objects and conditional filter() calls for flexible search
patterns_discovered.frequency: Used in order_list for search across multiple fields

gotchas_discovered.description: Decimal values converted from POST request strings using Decimal(str(value)) to avoid float precision issues
When creating order from purchase request, the PR status is automatically changed to 'ORDERED' without explicit user confirmation
gotchas_discovered.impact: Implicit state change that user may not expect

gotchas_discovered.description: Items can only be added/removed from DRAFT orders, but no check exists to prevent this if order transitions while user is editing
gotchas_discovered.impact: Race condition potential in concurrent edits

gotchas_discovered.description: No validation that quantity and unit_price are positive numbers or that material exists before creating item
gotchas_discovered.impact: Could allow invalid data (negative quantities, zero prices)

gotchas_discovered.description: Direct use of request.GET.get('page') without validation could cause PaginationError
gotchas_discovered.impact: get_page() handles invalid gracefully, but worth noting

gotchas_discovered.description: purchase_request_id assigned None only if falsy, but expected_delivery_date assigned as empty string default
Stats dictionary performs separate count() queries for each status, not optimized

approach_outcome.description: Create purchase_orders.py with all order views
approach_outcome.summary: Successfully implemented complete purchase order management views including list, detail, create, status transitions (send/confirm), and item management (add/remove). Implementation includes proper authentication, error handling, and database optimization patterns.
key_accomplishments: Query optimization with select_related and prefetch_related
Status-based access control for business logic
approach_outcome.approach_efficacy: High - Views are well-structured, follow Django conventions, and implement core business logic for purchase order workflow

recommendations.recommendation: Add validation in order_item_add to ensure quantity and unit_price are positive numbers before database insertion
recommendations.rationale: Prevents invalid data entry that could cause downstream issues in inventory calculations

recommendations.recommendation: Implement optimistic locking or SELECT FOR UPDATE on order status checks to prevent race conditions during concurrent edits
recommendations.rationale: Multiple users could edit same order simultaneously, causing status inconsistencies

recommendations.recommendation: Optimize stats calculation in order_list using aggregation (Count with filter) instead of separate count() calls
recommendations.rationale: Reduce database queries from 4 to 1 for statistics

recommendations.recommendation: Use more specific exception handling instead of generic Exception catches, log exceptions for debugging
recommendations.rationale: Generic catches mask underlying issues and make debugging difficult

recommendations.recommendation: Create Django Form classes for order_create and order_item_add to centralize validation logic
recommendations.rationale: Current validation scattered across view logic; forms would provide reusability and better error messages

recommendations.recommendation: Make purchase request status update (to 'ORDERED') explicit through parameter or add logging/notification
recommendations.rationale: Users should be aware that creating an order from a PR changes its status

recommendations.recommendation: Standardize null handling - use explicit None for all optional date/text fields instead of mixing with empty strings
recommendations.rationale: Consistency in null handling prevents subtle bugs and improves code clarity

recommendations.recommendation: Create comprehensive unit tests covering: status transitions, permission checks, item operations, purchase request linking
recommendations.rationale: Complex state machine logic needs test coverage to prevent regressions
